goal.what: Whoever builds or changes Pin, a person or an AI, makes it give its users what they come for: the person, a plan settled as they mean it before any work starts, asked only what is theirs; the maker AI, a design settled with the person that it builds the work on as given.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json goal: "Whoever builds or changes the product, a person or an AI, makes it give its users what they come for."

.rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:23 "Pin, a plugin of its own in ccpm, pins a plan down from its purpose: a design tree from the goal down, the user asked only what is theirs, one point at a time, nothing left assumed"

questions.what: Reading an objective, does the developer know which user the product is for and what that user gets from it?
Weighing a piece of work, can the developer tell which one objective it brings closer?
After a change, can the developer tell from the key results whether users came closer to the objective?
Weighing a change that shortens the lead time, can the developer tell whether it keeps how well the user gets what the objective says?
For each objective, can the developer follow, step by step, how its user goes from when they first need it to having what the objective says?
Building a step of a scenario, can the developer tell whether it waits for a person, is taken by an AI, or runs as a script?
Can the developer change how the product works inside, while its users see the same, and leave the document as it is?

decisions.what: Who comes to Pin with a goal of their own?
decisions.decided: Two users. The person: the one whose plan it is, who wants an AI to make what they mean. The maker AI: an AI that is to make a work for a person, such as a role of another plugin, and wants the work's design settled with that person before it builds. The AI that later makes the person's work from the design comes to Pin with no goal of its own, so it is no user. Differs from the old UX, which named Turn and rn as the second user.
grounds: ux.json Q1 step 1: "List each one who comes to the product with a goal of their own, a person or an AI, by the role they play."
plugins/pin/skills/down/SKILL.md:3 "also when a role is given a goal and questions to Pin down as a design tree."
plugins/pin/README.md:9 "Pin is also for a plugin that makes something for a person"

decisions.what: Which plugins may the document name, and what plan do the examples use?
decisions.decided: Pin only. The maker AI is named by its role, never by a plugin that uses Pin. The example plan is the person's own: their notes app `notes` gets JSON output on `notes list`. Differs from the old UX, which named Turn, rn and Turn's designer.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:23 "Turn and rn take it in by dependencies. Builds on none."

ux.json Q7 thinking: "the document says only what users mean to do, see and receive, so any design that gives them the same leaves it true." A plugin that uses Pin can change or go while Pin's users see the same.

decisions.what: How many objectives, and cut by what?
decisions.decided: Two, one for each user and gain. O1, the person's: the plan settled as they mean it, asked only what is theirs; a piece of work on what Pin asks, finds, settles and shows brings it closer. O2, the maker AI's: a design settled with the person through it, keeping what it settled, that it builds on as given; a piece of work on what the maker AI hands over, passes on and gets back brings it closer. Checked by ux.json Q2 step 2 on changes made or planned: the five lines a decision is put in, a fact shown alone, and a stopped run going on from its file each bring O1 closer; the person's answer carried back word for word, a point the maker AI settled kept as given, and a point its work found settled again each bring O2 closer.
grounds: ux.json Q2 step 1: "List each user and what each gets from the product, and give each pair one objective."
ux.json Q2 step 2: "Take each change planned or recently made that alters what a user gets, and name the one objective it brings closer."
plugins/pin/core/roles/pinner.md:106 "A point the one who started you settled is settled. Write it as given, and do not ask it again."
plugins/pin/core/roles/pinner.md:164 "The one who started you may come back with points to settle again, such as what its work found."

decisions.what: O1, as one line with the user as its subject and no mechanism
decisions.decided: O1: The person has every point of their plan settled as they mean it before any work starts, asked only what is theirs. Checked by ux.json Q1 step 3: the old O1, pinning the plan down and leaving nothing assumed, could all be done while the person is no better off, as a design tree full and confirmed can still hold a point otherwise than they mean it. "As they mean it" holds the gain: the work made from the plan needs no point of it explained again. Differs from the old O1.
grounds: ux.json Q1 step 2: "Write each one's objective as one sentence that fits on one line: that user as its subject, then a verb, its object and the context it is done in, with no feature or mechanism of the product."
ux.json Q1 step 3: "Ask whether the product could do all the sentence says while that user is no better off. If so, rewrite the sentence around what the user gains."

decisions.what: O2, as one line with the user as its subject and no mechanism
decisions.decided: O2: The maker AI has a work's design settled with the person it is for, keeping what it settled, and builds on it as given. Checked by ux.json Q1 step 3: the old O2, getting back a design tree it can build on, could be done while the maker AI still settles points with the person itself; "settled with the person it is for" and "builds on it as given" hold the gain, a design it need not settle itself. Differs from the old O2.
grounds: ux.json Q1 step 2, as for D4.
ux.json Q1 step 3, as for D4.

decisions.what: How do success and failure of each objective show in what the user does?
decisions.decided: O1 fails where the work needs a point the confirmed design does not hold or holds open, so the person explains it again or an assumption shows up later; where the design holds a point otherwise than the person means it, so the work is redone; where Pin asks the person a point that is not theirs, so they leave it to Pin or tell Pin a fact it could have found; and where the person works around Pin, settling a point in a chat with the AI that makes the work or writing the plan out themselves. O2 fails where the design holds otherwise a point the maker AI settled, or the person is asked it again; where a question the maker AI gave has no decision under it; where the maker AI answers or rewords a question meant for the person, as it cannot pass it on as given; and where the maker AI works around Pin, changing the design or settling a point with the person itself before or during the work.
grounds: ux.json Q3 step 1: "For the objective, list how success or failure would show in what the user does or feels, such as giving up, undoing a result or working around the product."
ux.json Q3 grounds, Rodden et al.: "Sometimes failure is easier to identify than success"

decisions.what: What does each key result count?
decisions.decided: For each objective, a share of what goes wrong, counted out of a named whole, with D6's ways listed under it; then a lead time from the user's request to the design they have. Lower and shorter are better. Checked by ux.json Q3 step 3: O1's ways count both a point missed or held wrong and a point asked that was not the person's, so KR1.1 cannot fall by asking the person everything, nor by settling everything without them; O2's ways count the maker AI working around Pin, so KR2.1 cannot fall while the maker AI still settles points with the person itself.
grounds: ux.json Q3 step 2: "Make each a share, an average per user, a count or a time, and name what it is counted out of."
ux.json Q3 step 3: "Ask whether all the objective's key results could get better while the user still does not get what the objective says. If so, add or rework key results until they could not."

decisions.decided: KR1.1: of the points of the plan, the share that goes wrong, a point being a decision the work turns out to need or a question put to the person, in D6's four ways for O1. KR1.2: the lead time from the person's first request to the design they confirm. Differs from the old KR1.1, which did not count a question that was not the person's or the person working around Pin.
grounds: D6
D7

decisions.decided: KR2.1: of the designs the maker AI gets back, the share that goes wrong, in D6's four ways for O2. KR2.2: the lead time from the maker AI's request to the design it gets back. Differs from the old KR2.1, which counted faults the check finds and not the maker AI working around Pin.
grounds: D6

decisions.what: How does the developer weigh a change that shortens the lead time?
decisions.decided: Said once under the OKRs: in each objective the first key result comes first, and a change shortens the lead time only if it keeps the first as good. Key results have no target values (Goodhart's law). The old line that all of ccpm aims at the same goes, as it names what Pin does not depend on and adds nothing to the rule.
grounds: ux.json Q4 thinking: "Quality first, then lead time"
ux.json Q4 steps: "Imagine the change, and ask whether it could make the first key result worse." "Keep it only where it could not."

decisions.what: Who takes part, and of what kind?
decisions.decided: The person (person), the maker AI (AI) and Pin (AI), one box for all Pin does, as Claude runs it. What runs inside Pin, such as its check and what finds a fact, is no participant. Each step from the person waits for the person. Differs from the old UX, which listed the main conversation, the researcher, check.py and Turn's designer.
grounds: ux.json Q6 step 1: "In each scenario, name each participant it uses, with its kind, as the list of participants gives them"
ux.json Q7 grounds, Cockburn: "For computer systems, it is rare that we open up the black box."

decisions.what: What does the document show, and what does it leave to the README and the architecture?
decisions.decided: Only what the person and the maker AI do, see and receive: the plan or the work's goal handed over, one point at a time to confirm or decide, the whole design to confirm, and the design kept in a file. How Pin finds a fact, how it checks the design, the file's form and the headings a message is passed under are inside the box. Checked by ux.json Q7 step 1 on one change, Pin run in a subagent instead of in the conversation that started it, finding each fact itself and checking the design by reading it instead of by a script: the line that put Pin in the conversation that started it was flagged and now says only that Claude runs Pin, and every other line stays true.
grounds: ux.json Q7 step 1: "Pick one change the design could make while users see the same, read every line, and flag each line that would have to change."
ux.json Q7 step 2: "Rewrite each flagged line by what the user does, sees or receives, or leave it to the document that describes the design inside"

decisions.what: How much does a step of a scenario say?
decisions.decided: Each arrow says in a few words what one does to another. The content passed, such as the five lines of a decision or the form of the file, is the spec, left to the README and the architecture. Differs from the old UX, whose arrows quoted whole messages.
grounds: ux.json Q5 step 2: "Write each step as one message, from the one who takes it to the one it acts on, saying what it passes, checks or changes"

decisions.decided: By its objective's ID and a short active phrase, the user its subject: "O1: The person settles the JSON output of notes list", "O2: The maker AI has the design of the JSON output settled".
grounds: ux.json Q5 step 1: "Name each scenario by its objective's ID and a short active verb phrase, the user its subject, saying how they reach it."

decisions.what: Where does each objective's gain show in its run?
decisions.decided: In a loop until no point is open: Pin settles itself each point that follows from the goal and the facts, and puts to the person one point alone, a fact it found to confirm or a decision of theirs with a recommendation. In O2 the same loop runs through the maker AI, and Pin keeps what the maker AI settled without asking it again. Without the loop, the scenario would read the same as a plan talked over in a chat, and the reader could not see what the user gains.
grounds: ux.json Q5 step 3: "Mark a part that repeats as a loop with its condition, holding each step that repeats."
ux.json Q5 step 4: "each step moves toward it."

decisions.decided: The person types /pin:down with the plan in their own words. Pin puts the goal to confirm, and the person says yes. The loop of D15 runs. Pin shows the whole design, each point in a short line with who settled it, and the person confirms they mean the same. Pin hands the person the design, kept in a file for the AI that makes the work.
grounds: ux.json Q5 step 4: "the first message is the user's request, the last gives the user the end"
plugins/pin/README.md:142 "Hand the file to the AI that makes"

decisions.decided: The maker AI starts Pin with the work's goal, the questions the work must answer, what it has settled and where to keep the design. Pin keeps what the maker AI settled, the goal among it. The loop of D15 runs through the maker AI, which passes each point to the person as given and the answer back word for word. Pin hands the whole design through the maker AI for the person to confirm, then hands the maker AI the design, kept where it said. The maker AI builds the work on it as given.
